discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in `1544b995b`. `suggestion()` in `candidates.ts` now clips `prompt` to `PROMPT_MAX_CHARS` and `why` to `WHY_MAX_CHARS` before it hashes the id, so rule, model and turn rows all stay inside the published bounds. Text within the limits is unchanged, so the `host-rules.json` parity fixtures keep their ids. `contracts.test.ts` builds rows from a long task title, a status headline and a failing check list, and validates the set and push against `NextTurnSet` and `NextTurnTrayPush`.

Fixed in 85ba54c1e8. When a Skip names a row that sits before the cursor (one New set already paged past), the cursor now moves back by one. Only the skipped row leaves the pool, and the rows on screen stay put. A test pins your sequence: New set, then a late Skip for Verify, leaves Review/Wrap up/Next step in view, and Undo skip brings Verify back to the front. I also fuzzed 4,000 random verb sequences offline against "a skip hides only its row, more drops only the last row, Undo skip brings its row into view". The fuzzer finds this bug without the fix and finds nothing with it.

agent feedback: The first three recovery tests cover the feature's main promises well: successful retry, truncation again, and nothing to compact. The tests from here onward mostly protect detailed telemetry behavior for listener errors, hooks, empty responses, and tool-call variants that the run loop already owns. If the telemetry contract is simplified to whether compaction/retry completed, I think these extra cases and much of their supporting implementation can be removed while preserving the important behavioral coverage.
